speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked	the Prime Minister (a) whether there is any risk assessment made by the Government on our vulnerability to foreign interference in our elections from both state and non-state actors; (b) what are the measures in place to safeguard Singapore from foreign interference in our elections; (c) what are the security guidelines on vigilance by political parties and candidates on this issue; and (d) how can the social media be kept free and open for political discussions whilst dealing with malicious/subversive content.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: History has shown that bigger and more powerful states would seek to advance their interests by projecting their influence on, usually, smaller or less well organised ones via all instruments of power, ranging from military, economic, cultural, diplomatic to informational.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We cannot expect to be immune from such external forces.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Singapore's small size, openness and relatively short history have always made it challenging for us to mitigate the external influences on our systems.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The advent of modern technologies, proliferation of various media platforms, rapid communication cycles and seamless information transmission channels combine to further complicate our task of defending ourselves from external influences.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our consistent position has always been that politics in Singapore is meant only for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We chart our own course and bear responsibilities for our choices.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have various existing measures to guard ourselves and our systems from foreign interference, but we will need to evolve them in tandem with the changes in technology, media platforms and communications channels.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, the Political Donations Act prohibits election candidates and political parties from accepting foreign funding.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Under the Societies Act, only Singapore citizens can be members of political associations and these associations must not have affiliation or connection with any organisation outside of Singapore that is contrary to our national interest.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Second, we have measures to protect Government networks and IT systems, so that they are not used by others to subvert our election process.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If these systems are compromised, they can be exploited to leak information or propagate fake news to disrupt election campaigns and shape voting patterns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Election candidates and political parties also need to safeguard their own systems.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If they require advice on the security of their IT systems, they can approach SingCERT, a division of the Cyber Security Agency.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Third, to prevent foreigners from manipulating our media platforms to influence local politics, the Newspaper and Printing Presses Act and the Broadcasting Act allow the Government to restrict and control the ownership of newspapers and broadcast media.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Funds from foreign sources for non-commercial purposes are prohibited for newspaper companies, broadcasting companies and corporatised online news entities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They can take the form of surreptitious contributions, which can be seemingly harmless donations to unsuspecting Singaporeans or local organisations, so that influence and pressure can be exerted over them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This threat of foreign influence is compounded by the pervasive use of the Internet and social media.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our Government agencies, such as the National Library Board and organisations like the Media Literacy Council, have also embarked on various programmes, such as the Better Internet, and the Source, Understand, Research and Evaluate programme, or SURE for short, to help Singaporeans become more discerning in what we read.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Nonetheless, the Government must also be able to step in to ensure that fake news which impacts society is not allowed to spread unchecked.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The integrity of our democratic process is the collective responsibility of all stakeholders and our electorate.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Each one of us must play our part by being vigilant and discerning about what we might have read or heard, in order to safeguard our democratic processes from being undermined by foreign influence.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Ultimately, our best defence is a discerning electorate that recognises the realities of geopolitics and the world which we live in.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Just wanted to check, would there be any measures that might be taken for the upcoming Presidential Election?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I understand that there would be more education on fake news, but what really can we do more to educate Singaporeans to be more vigilant to recognise fake news, but what really can we do more to educate Singaporeans to be more vigilant to recognise fake news?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On what more we can do, beyond what I have just stated, I think there are two other important things we need to do collectively as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, I think we need to be much more aware of the many teachable moments that are readily available in other parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are many lessons which we can draw from some of the recent episodes that have happened in other parts of the world; episodes that have happened to even bigger countries than us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many of such issues cannot be shared publicly and may not be in our best interest to share publicly, but, nevertheless, we must endeavour to share such things, where possible, in closed sessions with our community leaders so that we have a collective awareness of the world that we are living in and the geopolitical forces that we have to contend with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to need to be vigilant at the systems level but we will also need everyone to do this collectively, so that, collectively as Singaporeans, we can all do our part to safeguard the integrity of our own democratic processes, make the choices that we desire to make.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because, ultimately, we, as Singaporeans, will bear the collective responsibility for all the decisions that we have made.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Just two quick questions, to ask the Minister.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
